blocks.content: India experiences a monsoon type of climate characterized by seasonal reversal of winds, distinct wet and dry seasons, and large regional variations in temperature and rainfall. The climate of India is influenced by latitude, altitude, pressure systems, distance from the sea, and the Himalayan mountain range.
1. Factors Affecting Climate of India

blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: India's climate is broadly classified as tropical monsoon, heavily influenced by seasonal wind reversals.
The South-West Monsoon divides into two primary branches: the Arabian Sea Branch and the Bay of Bengal Branch.
Global atmospheric phenomena like El Niño and La Niña play a crucial role in altering the intensity of Indian rainfall.
Local winds in India vary regionally and significantly affect temperature and seasonal rainfall patterns prior to the monsoon.

blocks.content: • Latitude – India lies between 8°4′N and 37°6′N. Tropic of Cancer divides the country into tropical and subtropical parts.
• Altitude – High altitude regions such as Himalayas experience colder climates.
• Distance from Sea – Coastal areas have moderate climate while interior regions have extreme climate.
• Relief – Himalayas act as a barrier preventing cold winds from Central Asia.
• Monsoon Winds – Seasonal reversal of winds largely controls rainfall.
2. Seasons of India

cells: Cool temperatures, clear skies, western disturbances bring rainfall to north India
High temperatures, formation of low pressure areas, dust storms
Heavy rainfall due to moisture-laden winds from Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal
Withdrawal of monsoon winds; rainfall in Tamil Nadu

blocks.content: 3. Mechanism of Indian Monsoon
• During summer, intense heating of land creates low pressure over northern India.
• The Indian Ocean remains relatively cooler creating high pressure.
• Moist winds blow from sea to land bringing rainfall.
• The monsoon winds split into two branches: Arabian Sea branch and Bay of Bengal branch.
Branches of South-West Monsoon

cells: Strikes Western Ghats causing heavy rainfall in Kerala, Karnataka and Maharashtra
Moves toward northeast India and spreads across the Ganga plains

blocks.content: 4. Distribution of Rainfall in India
• Western Ghats and northeastern states receive very heavy rainfall.
• Regions like Rajasthan and Ladakh receive very low rainfall.

rows: Warming of eastern Pacific waters; weakens Indian monsoon rains and increases drought risk.
Cooling of eastern Pacific waters; strengthens Indian monsoon rains and brings above-average rainfall.

blocks.content: • Most rainfall occurs during the southwest monsoon season.
• Cherrapunji and Mawsynram in Meghalaya are among the wettest places in the world.
Climatic Regions of India

cells: Heavy rainfall throughout the year; found in Western Ghats and Northeast
Low rainfall; found in Rajasthan and parts of Deccan
Hot summers and cold winters; found in northern plains
Cold climate with snowfall; found in Himalayan region

blocks.content: 6. Important Local Winds in India
• Loo – Hot dry winds blowing in northern India during summer.
• Kal Baisakhi – Violent thunderstorms in eastern India.
• Mango Showers – Pre-monsoon showers in Kerala and Karnataka that help ripening of mangoes.
7. El Niño and La Niña Effect

items: Frequently tested: Differentiating between the Arabian Sea branch and Bay of Bengal branch of the SW Monsoon.
High yield: Identifying local seasonal winds (e.g., Loo, Kalbaisakhi, Mango Showers) and their respective regions.
Critical concept: The opposing effects of El Niño (drought risk) and La Niña (enhanced rainfall) on Indian monsoon behavior.

blocks.content: El Niño refers to warming of surface waters in the Pacific Ocean which weakens the Indian monsoon and may cause drought conditions. La Niña refers to cooling of Pacific waters and often strengthens the monsoon.
Important Facts
• Tropic of Cancer divides India into tropical and subtropical regions.
• Southwest monsoon brings most of India's rainfall.
• Mawsynram in Meghalaya receives the highest rainfall in the world.
• Loo winds occur during summer in northern India.
